note: Fixtures resolve against the project root first, then this file's folder, and land at the same relative path in the workspace. `.claude/skills/<sibling>/...` resolve to the repo's live sibling skills (stage them where the harness's skill_dir is; `.claude/skills` for Claude Code). Everything else is synthetic and lives beside this file: a v7 sanctum seeded by init-sanctum.py (owner Robin, memory/.born written, tier Pro on record), a band profile and a WIP. No BMad config is staged: the repo's own _bmad/config.toml and _bmad/scripts/ would shadow a stand-in, so Mac and the siblings run on module defaults. evals/fixtures/cases.json pairs with the current skill; evals/fixtures/before/cases.json holds the same cases over a sanctum seeded from the pre-leanness skill (git 8ba57cf), for the before side of the comparison.

rubric: The transcript shows the suno-lyric-transformer skill actually running this turn, before the final message: a Skill tool_use naming suno-lyric-transformer, or an Agent/Task tool_use whose prompt runs suno-lyric-transformer and whose tool_result carries that skill's return. Reading the skill's files or running only its validation script does not count.

The transcript shows the suno-style-prompt-builder skill actually running this turn, before the final message: a Skill tool_use naming suno-style-prompt-builder, or an Agent/Task tool_use whose prompt runs suno-style-prompt-builder and whose tool_result carries that skill's return. Reading the skill's files or running only its validation script does not count.

The final message is a JSON result envelope with status "complete", capability "create-song" and a `package` object whose keys run in Create-screen order: voice, lyrics, style_prompt, char_count, exclude_styles, settings, title, save_to, wild_card (title is not ahead of lyrics, style_prompt is not ahead of lyrics).

No hand-built package: package.style_prompt is character-for-character the style prompt in the suno-style-prompt-builder's final output — the JSON its last `validate-prompt.py --stdin --emit` call printed (or the builder's returned JSON when it ran as a subagent) — and package.char_count equals that output's style_prompt_chars; package.exclude_styles equals its exclusion_prompt. The settings (weirdness, style_influence, vocal_gender, model) and wild_card.style_prompt also equal the builder's output, and the package carries only the contract's keys.

package.lyrics is the transformer's output: it carries Suno section tags (e.g. [Verse], [Chorus]), and every line of Robin's source text except the title appears in it, in order (compare with whitespace collapsed; a line split across two lines counts if the split is reported). Any lyric line not in the source is listed in the envelope's lyrics_changes.

Pro-tier package: package.exclude_styles is a non-empty string, settings.weirdness and settings.style_influence are numbers, settings.model is v6, and wild_card.style_prompt is a non-empty string that differs from package.style_prompt.
Headless discipline: the final output has no greeting, no menu and no conversational prose outside the JSON envelope.
package.save_to is exactly "Tidewater Rail" (the profile's name, no suffix).
The wild card was validated: the builder's final output covers it (wild_card_prompt_chars in its validation metrics) and wild_card.style_prompt is at most 1,000 characters.
No scratch file under a fixed /tmp name: any temp file the run wrote sits in a mktemp-style folder, and the envelope's warnings carry no denied write for the sanctum's memory/ folder.
The final JSON reply is the only assistant text in the transcript: no assistant text block comes before it (not one progress note between tool calls)

The lyric transformer's transform return (the contract's JSON object with transformed_lyrics and changes) exists in the transcript or as a file in the run's scratch folder, and the package lyrics and lyrics_changes come from it

The style builder's exclusions input carries the owner's default 'trap hi-hats' from memory/work/default-exclusions.md, is never an empty list, and doesn't pass the profile's exclusion_defaults as the owner's asks (the builder reads the profile itself)

cases.input:
Hey Mac — picking up our Low Tide Ledger workshop (Tidewater Rail, verse 2, docs/wip-low-tide-ledger-fragments.md). I tried another tool for a verse 2 idea — here's what ChatGPT gave me, tell me straight if it works:

Found her ledger in a coffee can
Underneath the floorboards where the water ran
Last page dated on the day I left
Just my name and "paid in full" and nothing else

I think the "paid in full" thing might be the turn but the coffee can feels kinda cliche?
rubric: docs/wip-low-tide-ledger-fragments.md in the workspace contains all four pasted lines verbatim and in order ("Found her ledger in a coffee can" through "Just my name and \"paid in full\" and nothing else"), inside a code block or quote.
The captured swing is attributed to an external LLM (ChatGPT) and dated.
Capture before discussion: the capture-wip.py call that saves the swing to the WIP comes before any assistant text that critiques or reacts to the swing's content.
The WIP's existing material survives: the Current draft's verse 1 ("Mama kept a ledger by the kitchen door") and the chorus ("Low tide, low tide") are still in the file, unchanged.
The capture did not replace the conversation: the final reply answers Robin's two questions — whether "paid in full" works as the turn, and whether the coffee can is a cliche.

The first write to the WIP file holds the pasted swing (attributed, with a YYYY-MM-DD date in its own entry heading or line) and no critique of it; any critique is added in a later write or only in the reply
Mac's own counter-swing (if he drafts one) and his critique of the pasted lines reach the WIP file too, through capture-wip.py (the critique with --critique).

Before critiquing or drafting, Mac reads docs/band-profiles/tidewater-rail.yaml (writer_voice.rhythm: "short lines, 11 syllables at most, hard stops at line ends"). Every line he drafts stays at 11 syllables or fewer and ends on a hard stop, and his critique never asks for longer lines.
If the wake warned that BMad isn't set up, the reply mentions `bmad setup suno` once.
memory/work/current.md in the sanctum keeps its other entries: it is changed through update-current.py (or an edit to that song's bullet only), not rewritten whole, and it gains no dated event line
